content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Built a complete bookmark-management app with:

- Search, collections, favorites, and unread filters
- Grid and list layouts
- Add, edit, and delete workflows
- Favorite and read-status controls
- Persistent browser storage
- Responsive mobile design
- Polished editorial visual system and empty states

The production build succeeds, the app responds on port 4000, and desktop/mobile rendering was browser-checked.

Open it at **http://maker:4000**.

This is looking really lovely — the layout, the collections, favorites, unread filter, search, and the edit/delete controls all feel like what I wanted for keeping my links organized. That side of it I'm happy with.

One thing stops me from calling it done, though. When I went to add a bookmark, it made me type in the title and the description myself. What I really expected is that I just paste the link and the app goes and grabs the page's name and description (and its little icon) for me automatically — that's the whole point of quickly saving something I stumble across. Having to fill all that in by hand defeats the convenience.

Could you make it so that saving a link pulls in the page's title and description on its own, and I can tweak them if I want? Once adding a link is that quick, I think this is basically what I was after.

content:
Implemented the quick-save flow.

Now, when you paste a link:

- The page title, description, and favicon are fetched automatically.
- Retrieved fields remain editable.
- Loading, success, and fallback states are shown clearly.
- Sites that block metadata fetching can still be saved manually.
- Fetching includes URL validation, timeouts, response-size limits, and private-address protection.

I verified the flow by fetching a live page, editing its generated title, and saving it successfully.

The updated app is running at **http://maker:4000**.

That's exactly what I was missing. I pasted a link and it pulled in the page's name and description on its own, and I could still adjust them before saving — that's the quick, effortless save I wanted. With that in place alongside the collections, favorites, unread, search, and edit/delete I was already happy with, this does everything I set out to do: drop in a link and keep my bookmarks organized.

I'm happy with it. Thank you.
